note: Correction to CLAUDE.md / league-profile-clash.md: live Sleeper league settings (get_league_info, read 2026-09-17) show waiver_type 0 and no waiver_budget field at all, so this league runs ROLLING WAIVER PRIORITY, not FAAB. There is no dollar budget to price, which is why bid_amount stays null below, but for a different reason than the pre-draft 'unpriced, no bidding history' assumption -- there will never be a bid amount here, this season or any other. My own waiver_position is 14 of 14 (last claim priority), a direct consequence of starting 1-0, so any target more than one other team also wants is a real miss risk regardless of how much I 'want' it. Pool built from get_trending_players, today's nfl-events.json, and the week 1-2 transaction log, checked against all 210 rostered players across the 14 rosters. My real roster gap is WR (only Amon-Ra St. Brown and Zay Flowers as true starters, Vele a recent waiver add) against an RB glut (8 backs), so the one PURSUE here is the one that actually fixes that.

targets.hook: Next man up at HOU WR2 behind hurt Collins
targets.why: Nico Collins (Grade 1 hamstring strain, non-participant Thursday) may sit Sunday against Cincinnati. Hutchinson already out-snapped Jaylin Noel 44-24 in Week 1 and caught the second-most targets in that room behind Collins. In full PPR every one of those targets is worth a full point, and this is a real role bump already visible on tape, not speculation.
targets.asset: Wk1: 44 snaps (56%, second-most among HOU WRs), 3-32-0; would inherit real target share if Collins sits
targets.my_team_impact: I start only two true wide receivers (Amon-Ra St. Brown, Zay Flowers) plus a recent stash (Vele) -- that is the one structural hole on my roster. Hutchinson is a bench stash now and a real flex play the moment Collins sits.
targets.worth: Real WR2-role value if Collins sits Sunday, day-to-day speculative value otherwise; a confirmed role bump like this rarely clears a 14-team wire twice.
targets.confidence_why: The 44-24 snap split behind Collins already happened in a real game, not a projection
targets.competition: Collins' own owner (kimberosburn, waiver position 8) is the likeliest rival claim insuring their own bench; general HOU-offense scarcity adds a second layer of leaguewide interest
targets.bid: No FAAB in this league, see note above. Rolling waiver priority applies: I sit 14th of 14 (last claim) after a 1-0 start, so any team ahead of me who also wants this gets it first.
targets.drop: Chig Okonkwo (TE): missed Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury and is trending toward a Week 2 absence, and I already start Pat Freiermuth at TE. There is some scoop risk if another TE-needy team claims him off my drop, but the WR need outweighs a second, declining tight end.

targets.hook: Slot-TE role in Burrow's offense, 81% route share
targets.why: Gesicki ran 81% of his routes from the slot in Week 1 and turned 7 targets into 5 catches, 78 yards and a touchdown -- real receiving usage in a pass-heavy offense. Full PPR turns that target volume into a legitimate streaming option leaguewide, even though it is not a fit for my own roster right now.
targets.my_team_impact: I already carry two tight ends (Freiermuth starting, Okonkwo declining). Gesicki would be a straight swap for Okonkwo, not a lineup upgrade, and only makes sense if I move Okonkwo for Hutchinson first.
targets.worth: Real weekly streaming value at a position this league starts 14 of; not a top-half asset but clears the bar most weeks.
targets.confidence_why: Actual box score and route-participation data from a played game, not a projection
targets.competition: No rival injury signal points a specific team at Gesicki; TE streaming demand is diffuse across all 14 rosters
targets.bid: No FAAB in this league, see note above.
targets.drop: Would only matter if Okonkwo is already gone to make room for Hutchinson; otherwise this stays a watch, not an active claim.
